newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH BANKERS SEE CREDIT GROWTH - ASSOCIATION.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH BANKERS SEE CREDIT GROWTH - ASSOCIATION.

text.p: Almost 90 percent of Finnish bankers expect household credit demand to grow in the fourth quarter after 84 percent experienced year-on-year growth in the third quarter, the Finnish Bankers' Association said on Monday.

In a new banking barometre which polled 281 managers at at Merita Bank, the cooperative banks, state-owned Postipankki and the savings banks in September, 88 percent of lenders to households expected growth in the fourth quarter.
Among lenders to corporations, 79 percent expected growth in credit demand, the assocition said in a statement.
On deposits, expectations were about equally distributed over the three categories -- growth, unchanged and decline. However, a 57 percent majority said deposits were a declining form of investment.

On the other hand, a full 99 percent saw growth in individual savings insurance and 75 percent saw growth in real estate investment among households. 65 percent expected investment in bonds and interest rate funds to increase whereas a majority expected equity investment to be unchanged in the fourth quarter.
